'''Miroslav Raduljica''' ({{Langx|sr|Мирослав Радуљица}}; born 5 January 1988)<ref name="Biografija"/> is a Serbian former professional [[basketball]] player. He currently plays as a [[Forward (association football)|forward]] for FK Železničar Inđija of the [[Serbian SuperLiga]]. Raduljica has also represented the [[Serbia men's national basketball team|Serbian national team]] in international competitions. Standing at {{Height|m=2.13}}, Raduljica plays at the [[Center (basketball)|center]] position.

==Professional career==
===Early careers in Serbia and Turkey===
Raduljica began his career playing with the [[KK FMP (1991–2011)|KK FMP]] junior teams in Serbia. He made his professional debut with FMP during the 2005–06 season. Raduljica spent the 2006–07 season on loan at [[KK Borac Čačak]] and then moved back to FMP.
On 8 July 2010, Raduljica signed a five-year contract with Turkish club [[Anadolu Efes S.K.|Efes Pilsen]],<ref>{{Cite web|title=Efes Pilsen locks up Radulica for 5 years|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/73556/180/item|url-status=dead|website=Euroleague|date=8 July 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110615160213/http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/73556/180/item|archive-date=15 June 2011}}</ref> but moved to [[Alba Berlin]] on loan during the season, with which he reached the finals of the German [[Basketball Bundesliga|Bundesliga]]. On 25 August 2011, Raduljica moved to [[KK Partizan|Partizan]] on loan for one season.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Partizan takes Raduljica on loan from Efes|url=http://www.euroleague.net/euroleaguenews/transactions/2011-12-signings/i/87328/5611/partizan-takes-raduljica-on-loan-from-efes|url-status=dead|website=Euroleague|date=31 August 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111001024211/http://www.euroleague.net/euroleaguenews/transactions/2011-12-signings/i/87328/5611/partizan-takes-raduljica-on-loan-from-efes|archive-date=1 October 2011}}</ref> On 22 September 2012, Raduljica moved to Ukrainian club [[BC Azovmash|Azovmash]] on a one-season loan.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Azovmash Mariupol gets Miroslav Raduljica|url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/ukraine/43949/azovmash-mariupol-gets-miroslav-raduljica.html|url-status=dead|website=Sportando|date=22 September 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130103194912/http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/ukraine/43949/azovmash-mariupol-gets-miroslav-raduljica.html|archive-date=3 January 2013}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Raduljica prešao u Azovmaš|url=http://www.b92.net/sport/kosarka/vesti.php?yyyy=2012&mm=09&dd=22&nav_id=645208|website=[[B92]]|date=22 September 2012|access-date=29 June 2026|language=sr}}</ref>

===NBA and China===
On 26 July 2013, Raduljica signed with the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] of the [[National Basketball Association]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Bucks Sign Free-Agent Center Miroslav Raduljica|url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/release/bucks-sign-free-agent-center-miroslav-raduljica|publisher=NBA|date=26 July 2013|access-date=29 June 2026}}</ref> In his debut season, he played sparingly for the 15-67 Bucks, earning just 9.7 minutes per match on average. In 48 matches, Raduljica earned 3.8 points and 2.3 rebounds on average per match.<ref>{{Cite web|title=2013-14 Milwaukee Bucks Roster and Stats|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/teams/MIL/2014.html|website=Basketball Reference|access-date=29 June 2026}}</ref> On 26 August 2014, along with [[Carlos Delfino]] and a 2015 second round draft pick, Raduljica wast traded to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] in exchange for [[Jared Dudley]] and a 2017 conditional first round draft pick.<ref>{{Cite web|first=Robyn|last=Dixon|title=Clippers Acquire Carlos Delfino and Miroslav Raduljica |url=https://www.nba.com/clippers/press-release-delfino-raduljica|url-status=dead|publisher=NBA|date=26 August 2014|access-date=30 August 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150627203533/https://www.nba.com/clippers/press-release-delfino-raduljica|archive-date=27 June 2015}}</ref> On 29 August 2014, he was waived by the Clippers.<ref>{{Cite web|first=Karen|last=Song|title=Clippers Waive Carlos Delfino And Miroslav Raduljica |url=https://www.nba.com/clippers/clippers-waive-carlos-delfino-and-miroslav-raduljica|url-status=dead|publisher=NBA|date=29 August 2014|access-date=29 August 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150612204241/https://www.nba.com/clippers/clippers-waive-carlos-delfino-and-miroslav-raduljica|archive-date=12 June 2015}}</ref>

On 19 September 2014, Raduljica signed a one-year contract with the [[Shandong Lions]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]], with a guaranteed price of $1.5 million.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Miroslav Raduljica tweets he has signed with Shandong |url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/135160/miroslav-raduljica-tweets-he-has-signed-with-shandong.html|url-status=dead|website=Sportando|date=19 September 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150711023312/https://sportando.com/en/world/asia/135160/miroslav-raduljica-tweets-he-has-signed-with-shandong.html|archive-date=11 July 2015}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|first=Nick|last=Bedard|title=Miroslav Raduljica cashed out of China, next stop NBA?|url=http://basketballbuddha.com/miroslav-raduljica-cashes-out-of-china-next-stop-nba/|url-status=dead|website=Basketball Buddha|date=23 December 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150103005030/http://basketballbuddha.com/miroslav-raduljica-cashes-out-of-china-next-stop-nba/|archive-date=3 January 2015}}</ref> On 23 December 2014, his contract was bought out by Shandong for $1.2 million.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Miroslav Raduljica gets a $1.2M buyout and leaves Shangdong|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/145937/miroslav-raduljica-gets-a-dollars12m-buyout-and-leaves-shangdong.html|access-date=23 December 2014|website=Sportando|date=23 December 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150711023312/https://sportando.com/en/world/asia/135160/miroslav-raduljica-tweets-he-has-signed-with-shandong.html|archive-date=11 July 2015}}</ref> In 14 matches, he earned 18 points and 9 rebounds on average per match.

===Return to NBA===
On 8 January 2015, Raduljica signed a ten-day contract with the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Timberwolves Sign Center Miroslav Raduljica to 10-Day Contract |url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/timberwolves-sign-center-miroslav-raduljica-to-10-day-contract |access-date=8 January 2015|publisher=NBA|date=8 January 2015}}</ref> On 19 January 2015, he signed another ten-day contract with the club.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Wolves Sign Center Miroslav Raduljica to Second 10-Day Contract |url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/wolves-sign-center-miroslav-raduljica-second-10-day-contract |access-date=20 January 2015|publisher=NBA|date=19 January 2015}}</ref> On 28 January, he was waived by the Timberwolves after appearing in five matches.<ref>{{cite news |title=Wolves Sign Guard Lorenzo Brown to a 10-Day Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/wolves-sign-guard-lorenzo-brown-10-day-contract |access-date=28 January 2015|publisher=NBA|date=28 January 2015}}</ref>

===Mediterranean career and China return===
On 18 July 2015, Raduljica signed a two-year contract with Greek club [[Panathinaikos B.C.|Panathinaikos]].<ref>{{Cite web|script-title=el:Συμφωνία με Ραντούλιτσα|url=http://www.paobc.gr/page.ashx?pid=2&aid=43546|url-status=dead|access-date=18 July 2015|website=Panathinaikos B.C.|date=18 July 2015|language=el|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304114838/http://www.paobc.gr/page.ashx?pid=2&aid=43546|archive-date=4 March 2016}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Panathinaikos tabs big man Raduljica |url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/67k8dwl7qtme3uhl|url-status=dead|website=Euroleague|date=18 July 2015|access-date=18 July 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304222241/http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/67k8dwl7qtme3uhl|archive-date=4 March 2016}}</ref> On 4 December 2015, he had a personal career single match scoring high in [[EuroLeague]], with 25 points against [[FC Barcelona Bàsquet|Barcelona]] in a 93–86 home victory.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Diamantidis, Raduljica lead Panathinaikos past Barcelona|url=http://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame?gamecode=93&seasoncode=E2015|url-status=dead|website=Euroleague|date=4 December 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160115043326/http://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame?gamecode=93&seasoncode=E2015#!report#!report|archive-date=15 January 2016}}</ref> After one season, he parted ways with the team.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Miroslav Raduljica, Panathinaikos agreed to part ways|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/greece/203890/miroslav-raduljica-panathinaikos-agreed-to-part-ways.html|url-status=dead|website=Sportando|date=28 June 2016|access-date=28 June 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170511053342/https://sportando.com/en/europe/greece/203890/miroslav-raduljica-panathinaikos-agreed-to-part-ways.html|archive-date=11 May 2017}}</ref>

On 15 July 2016, Raduljica signed another two-year contract, this time with Italian club [[Pallacanestro Olimpia Milano|EA7 Emporio Armani Milano]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Olimpia Milano signs Miroslav Raduljica|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/italy/serie-a/206423/olimpia-milano-signs-miroslav-raduljica.html |access-date=15 July 2016|website=Sportando|date=15 July 2016}}</ref> After one season, he left Milano.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Olimpia Milano parting ways|url=https://sportando.com/en/italy/serie-a/206423/olimpia-milano-signs-miroslav-raduljica.html|url-status=dead|website=Sportando|date=15 July 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160820165106/https://sportando.com/en/italy/serie-a/206423/olimpia-milano-signs-miroslav-raduljica.html|archive-date=20 August 2016}}</ref> On 9 June 2017, he signed with the [[Jiangsu Dragons]] of the Chinese Basketball Association.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Miroslav Raduljica signs in China with Jiangsu Dragons|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/236546/miroslav-raduljica-signs-in-china-with-jiangsu-dragons.html|url-status=dead|website=Sportando|date=9 June 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170613040704/http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/236546/miroslav-raduljica-signs-in-china-with-jiangsu-dragons.html|archive-date=13 June 2017}}</ref> Raduljica earned 25.4 points and 9.8 rebounds per game in the 2019–20 season on average. On 3 September 2020, he signed with [[Zhejiang Lions]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=Borghesan|first=Ennio Terrasi|title=Zhejiang Lions, Miroslav Raduljica agree to deal |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/zhejiang-lions-miroslav-raduljica-agree-to-deal/|website=Sportando |access-date=3 September 2020 |date=3 September 2020}}</ref>

===Later career===
In July 2021, Raduljica signed for the [[Goyang Orion Orions|Goyang Orions]] of the [[Korean Basketball League]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Miroslav Raduljica nastavlja karijeru u Južnoj Koreji|url=https://www.mozzartsport.com/kosarka/vesti/miroslav-raduljica-nastavlja-karijeru-u-juznoj-koreji/394361|website=Mozzart Sport|date=29 July 2021|access-date=29 June 2021|language=sr}}</ref> On 11 December, he was waived after earning 8.6 points and 5.3 rebounds per match on average.<ref>{{Cite web|first=Dario|last=Skerlecic|title=Goyang Orions sign Marcus Derrickson, release Miroslav Raduljica|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/goyang-orions-sign-marcus-derrickson-release-miroslav-raduljica/|website=Sportando|date=11 December 2021|access-date=29 June 2026}}</ref>

In September 2022, Raduljica signed for 2022–23 campaign back home with [[KK Crvena zvezda]].{{cn|date=July 2026}} He left the club on 4 September 2023.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Crvena Zvezda part ways with Miroslav Raduljica|url=https://basketnews.com/news-194245-crvena-zvezda-part-ways-with-miroslav-raduljica.html|website=Basket News|date=4 September 2023|access-date=29 June 2026}}</ref> Three days later, on 7 September, Raduljica re-signed for [[Maroussi B.C.|Maroussi]] of the [[Greek Basketball League]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Raduljica re-signs at Maroussi|url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Greece/news/884085/Raduljica-re-signs-at-Maroussi|website=Eurobasket|date=27 July 2024|access-date=29 July 2024}}</ref> On 27 February 2025, he and Maroussi mutually agree to part ways.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Miroslav Raduljica se rastao sa Marusijom: Grci zahvalni Srbinu kao niko do sad|url=https://www.telegraf.rs/sport/kosarka/4063343-miroslav-raduljica-se-rastao-sa-marusijom-grci-zahvalni-srbinu-kao-niko-do-sad|website=Telegraf|date=27 February 2025|access-date=29 June 2026|language=sr}}</ref>

==Serbian national team==
{{see also|2016 Serbia men's Olympic basketball team|2014 Serbia FIBA Basketball World Cup team}}
[[File:Miroslav Raduljica (battle of two centres).jpg|150px|thumb|left|Miroslav Raduljica (left) vs [[Jure Balažič]] ]]
Raduljica played with the Serbian junior national teams, having won gold medals at the [[2005 FIBA Europe Under-18 Championship]], the [[2007 FIBA Under-19 World Championship]], as well as the [[2008 FIBA Europe Under-20 Championship]] where he was named the MVP.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Raduljica Named MVP|url=http://www.fibaeurope.com/cid_KNce8jInH7Qj1EsyH5rjn2.season_2008.compID_UIfgjyQcGqk-fPlnl66Tj0.coid_e-W9nS5yGPwOEXedgwlPW2.articleMode_on.html|url-status=dead|publisher=FIBA|date=10 August 2008|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090731145120/http://www.fibaeurope.com/cid_KNce8jInH7Qj1EsyH5rjn2.season_2008.compID_UIfgjyQcGqk-fPlnl66Tj0.coid_e-W9nS5yGPwOEXedgwlPW2.articleMode_on.html|archive-date=31 July 2009}}</ref>

Raduljica also played with the [[Serbia men's national basketball team|senior team]] that won the silver medal at the [[EuroBasket 2009]] and [[2014 FIBA Basketball World Cup]], the latter under head coach [[Aleksandar Đorđević]]. Over nine tournament matches, he earned 13 points and 4.6 rebounds in 21 minutes per match on average.<ref>{{cite web |title=Miroslav Raduljica|url=https://www.fiba.basketball/basketballworldcup/2014/player/Miroslav-Raduljica |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190203202120/http://www.fiba.basketball/basketballworldcup/2014/player/Miroslav-Raduljica |url-status=live |archive-date=3 February 2019|publisher=FIBA|access-date=15 September 2014}}</ref>

He represented Serbia again at the [[EuroBasket 2015]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Ambitious Serbia Unveil Powerful 12-Man Squad|url=http://www.eurobasket2015.org/en/compID_qMRZdYCZI6EoANOrUf9le2.season_2015.roundID_9322.coid_xUMkR0x,HeIT9w-vv9Ob00.articleMode_on.html |access-date=3 September 2015|website=Eurobasket 2015|date=2 September 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150905064710/http://www.eurobasket2015.org/en/compID_qMRZdYCZI6EoANOrUf9le2.season_2015.roundID_9322.coid_xUMkR0x,HeIT9w-vv9Ob00.articleMode_on.html |archive-date=5 September 2015 |url-status=usurped}}</ref> In the first phase of the tournament, Serbia dominated in the tournament's toughest group, [[EuroBasket 2015 Group B|Group B]], with a 5–0 record, then eliminated [[Finland national basketball team|Finland]] and [[Czech Republic national basketball team|Czech Republic]] in the round of 16 and quarterfinal matches, respectively. However, they were beaten 67–64 in the semifinal match by [[Lithuania men's national basketball team|Lithuania]],<ref>{{Cite web|title=Lithuania End Serbian Streak, Return to Final|url=http://www.eurobasket2015.org/en/gameID_11664-76-A-1.html|website=Eurobasket 2015|access-date=20 September 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150919004022/http://www.eurobasket2015.org/en/gameID_11664-76-A-1.html |archive-date=19 September 2015 |url-status=dead}}</ref> and eventually lost against the host team, [[France national basketball team|France]] in the third place play-off by a score of 81–68.<ref>{{cite news |title=France Reward Home Support with Bronze|url=http://www.eurobasket2015.org/en/compID_qMRZdYCZI6EoANOrUf9le2.season_2015.roundID_9322.coid_XCBBt0,vHwcDLI3DN0sTU1.articleMode_on.html |access-date=20 September 2015 |website=Eurobasket 2015|date=20 September 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150922234352/http://www.eurobasket2015.org/en/compID_qMRZdYCZI6EoANOrUf9le2.season_2015.roundID_9322.coid_XCBBt0,vHwcDLI3DN0sTU1.articleMode_on.html |archive-date=22 September 2015 |url-status=usurped}}</ref> Being a starting [[center (basketball)|center]], and one of the team's along with [[Miloš Teodosić]] and [[Nemanja Bjelica]], Raduljica averaged 13.5 points and 5.0 rebounds, on 61.7% shooting from the field, in 9 tournament games; playing 18 minutes on average.<ref>{{cite web |title=Player profile: Miroslav Raduljica |url=http://www.eurobasket2015.org/en/compID_qMRZdYCZI6EoANOrUf9le2.season_2015.roundID_9322.teamID_96799.playerID_47677.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150905030047/http://www.eurobasket2015.org/en/compID_qMRZdYCZI6EoANOrUf9le2.season_2015.roundID_9322.teamID_96799.playerID_47677.html|url-status=dead|publisher=FIBA|access-date=20 September 2015|archive-date=5 September 2015}}</ref>

Raduljica also represented Serbia at the [[Basketball at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2016 Summer Olympics]] where they won the silver medal, after losing to the [[United States men's national basketball team|United States]] in the final game with 96–66.<ref>{{cite news |title=Rio Olympics 2016: USA beat Serbia in men's basketball to win last gold of Games |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/olympics/36727948|access-date=18 September 2017|website=[[BBC Sport]]|date=21 August 2016}}</ref>

At the [[2019 FIBA Basketball World Cup]], the national team of Serbia was dubbed as favorite team to win the trophy,<ref>{{Cite web|first=Igor|last=Curkovic|title=FIBA Basketball World Cup Power Rankings (Volume 3)|url=http://www.fiba.basketball/basketballworldcup/2019/news/fiba-basketball-world-cup-power-rankings-volume-3 |access-date=14 September 2019|publisher=FIBA|date=28 August 2019}}</ref> but eventually lost the [[2019 FIBA Basketball World Cup final round|quarterfinals]] against [[Argentina national basketball team|Argentina]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Argentina upsets Olympic silver medalist Serbia in FIBA World Cup quarterfinals |url=https://olympics.nbcsports.com/2019/09/10/argentina-serbia-fiba-world-cup/ |access-date=14 September 2019|website=NBC Sports|date=10 September 2019}}</ref> With victories against the [[United States men's national basketball team|United States]] and [[Czech Republic national basketball team|Czech Republic]], it finished in fifth place.<ref>{{cite news |title=Serbia defeats USA in FIBA World Cup consolation round play|url=https://www.nba.com/article/2019/09/12/fiba-world-cup-usa-serbia-game-recap|publisher=NBA|access-date=14 September 2019|date=12 September 2019}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Bogdanović ponovo briljirao – Srbiji peto mesto u Kini |url=https://www.b92.net/sport/kina2019/vesti.php?nav_id=1591176 |access-date=14 September 2019 |date=14 September 2019 |language=sr}}</ref> Raduljica was named the team's captain due to absence of Teodosić. In seven tournament matches, he earned 6.1 points, 2.1 rebounds, and 1.6 assists on average.

==Football career==
On 19 September 2025, Raduljica announced that he signed for FK Železničar Inđija in the [[Serbian League Vojvodina]], with all of his salary going to charity.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Miroslav Raduljica switches from decorated basketball career to football|url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/others/1870271/miroslav-raduljica-switches-to-football-serbia/|website=Eurohoops|date=19 September 2025|access-date=23 December 2025}}</ref> On 2 November, he made his football debut in the 12th round of a league match against [[GFK Sloven Ruma]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Ludilo: Miroslav Raduljica debituje kao fudbaler {{En dash}} pogledajte scene o kojima bruji Srbija! (Video)|url=https://sportissimo.republika.rs/fudbal/aktuelno/61862/miroslav-raduljica-zeleznicar-indjija-srpska-liga|website=sportissimo.republika.rs|date=2 November 2025|access-date=29 June 2026|language=sr}}</ref>

==Personal life==
In July 2022, Raduljica married his girlfriend, volleyball player Tamara Ignjić.<ref>{{Cite web|first=Slavica|last=Jovanović|title=Evo ko je izabranica košarkaša Miroslava Raduljice: Živela u Americi, bavi se odbojkom i veoma je uspešna|url=https://www.telegraf.rs/jetset/vesti-jetset/3531410-evo-ko-je-izabranica-kosarkasa-miroslava-raduljice-zivela-u-americi-bavi-se-odbojkom-i-veoma-je-uspesna|website=Telegraf|date=24 July 2022|access-date=29 June 2026|language=sr}}</ref> They welcomed their child in June 2024 <ref>{{Cite web|title=Miroslav Raduljica postao otac: Dobio sina i dao mu je čuveno srpsko ime!|url=https://www.telegraf.rs/sport/kosarka/3908555-miroslav-raduljica-postao-otac-dobio-sina-i-dao-mu-je-cuveno-srpsko-ime|website=Telegraf|date=12 June 2024|access-date=29 June 2026|language=sr}}</ref>
